caption: The drawing depicts an architectural interior focused on a symmetrical altar or decorative wall section. The central section is composed of three vertical panels, bordered by four columns decorated with floral patterns in pale pink, blue, and green. Each panel has a central niche or shelf; the larger central one has an ornate, fan-shaped element, while the two flanking niches have simpler bracketed supports with similar decorative motifs. The wall panels and architectural elements are painted in light pastel shades, predominately pale green with accents in blue, pink, gold, and beige. Above the panels is an entablature with repeated floral or geometric patterns, supporting two urns or vases on plinths, one on each side, decorated with blue, red, and gold elements. In the center at the top, a large stylized sunburst radiates outward, emerging from a cloud-like shape with a golden triangle in the middle. Behind the altar and columns, the wall is rendered in light wood tones with visible grain. On either side of the composition, the adjoining walls display patterned wallpaper in muted yellows and blues, creating a framed backdrop to the central architectural feature. The overall drawing employs fine detailing, precise linework, and a limited color palette emphasizing light pastel hues and ornamental details.
title: Decorations on Reredos and Sanctuary Walls
cluster: #12 — Spanish Colonial Art of the Southwest
